description:
Link Space is a multidisciplinary team passionate about software development, space exploration, and innovative technology. We aim to combine our technical and creative skills to develop meaningful solutions that address real-world challenges in human space exploration.

Our mission is to build innovative software that supports astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions, helping astronauts better understand their health indicators and make informed decisions.
summary:
VITALIS is an astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions. It brings health records, laboratory results, radiation records, exercise data, and wellbeing information into one unified workspace.

VITALIS uses a structured ten-stage workflow to validate incoming data, analyze personal health trends, generate preliminary assessments, cross-check evidence, and route reports to the assigned medical officer for human review.

The platform also provides role-based dashboards for astronauts, medical officers, and mission supervisors, alongside health alerts, wellness tools, cognitive games, and supported offline data synchronization.

Its key innovation is combining health information with data-quality checks, transparent evidence, and human medical oversight, helping users distinguish reliable information from incomplete or suspicious records.

VITALIS is a research and demonstration prototype, not a certified medical device or diagnostic system. Simulated health records are clearly identified, while NASA OSDR research metadata supports a separate educational research feature.
details:
VITALIS is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform developed to address the challenges of maintaining crew health during long-duration space missions.

The platform provides three main user roles:

  1. Astronaut: Accesses personal health dashboards, medical records, health trends, alerts, exercise tracking, and wellbeing features.
  2. Medical Officer: Reviews assigned astronauts' health records, preliminary assessments, alerts, medical reports, and follow-up decisions.
  3. Mission Supervisor: Oversees system operations, demonstration scenarios, synchronization status, and audit records.

CORE TECHNOLOGY AND WORKFLOW

VITALIS uses a ten-stage health analysis workflow:

  • Collects available health, laboratory, radiation, exercise, and wellbeing records.
  • Checks data quality and identifies missing or suspicious measurements.
  • Analyzes historical trends and individual baselines.
  • Generates a preliminary interpretation using the configured analysis engine.
  • Cross-checks the assessment against available medical reference information.
  • Independently verifies evidence, consistency, and data provenance.
  • Produces a structured assessment with uncertainty and supporting evidence.
  • Routes the report to the assigned medical officer.
  • Requires a qualified human medical professional to review and make decisions.
  • Records audit information and supported synchronization evidence.

INNOVATION AND IMPACT

The key innovation is integrating health monitoring with data-quality validation, evidence verification, and human-supervised decision support. Rather than treating every incoming measurement as reliable, VITALIS highlights incomplete or suspicious records and preserves uncertainty.

The platform also includes VITALIS LIFE, which provides wellbeing tools, exercise features, family communication, and six cognitive and engagement games. The Demo Center offers ten repeatable scenarios to demonstrate different health and data-quality situations.

TECHNOLOGIES USED

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS.
Backend: Node.js and Express.js.
Database: SQLite.
Other technologies include REST APIs, role-based access control, authentication, data visualization, Progressive Web App functionality, and SHA-256 integrity verification.

NASA DATA AND LIMITATIONS

VITALIS connects to NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), specifically the OSD-575 Inspiration4 study metadata, for research questions in the Games Arena. This is not a live astronaut vital-sign feed.

Health measurements displayed in the prototype are simulated and clearly identified as demonstration data. Physical medical sensors and operational NASA telemetry are not connected.

VITALIS is a research and demonstration prototype. It does not diagnose diseases, prescribe treatments, or replace qualified medical professionals.
